citation: Charlson ES et al. Topographical continuity of bacterial populations in the healthy human respiratory tract.
journal_year: Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2011
specimen: Oral/nasopharyngeal samples; serial BAL; protected brush; procedural controls
central_scientific_question: Are healthy lower-airway communities distinct from upper-airway communities?
main_finding: Lung sequences were 2–4 logs lower in biomass and largely resembled upper-airway flora.
conceptual_contribution: Established low biomass and mouth–lung continuity as first-order interpretation problems.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Supports an immigration/low-signal framework, not disease-specific taxa; compare BAL composition with independently sampled oral reference communities and procedural controls.
must_not_claim: Our BAL taxa prove resident colonization or aspiration.

citation: Morris A et al. Comparison of the respiratory microbiome in healthy nonsmokers and smokers.
journal_year: Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2013
central_scientific_question: How does the healthy lung relate to the mouth, and does smoking alter it?
main_finding: Most lung taxa were also oral; some taxa were overrepresented relative to neutral expectations; lung communities did not differ clearly by smoking.
conceptual_contribution: Showed that oral immigration is important but not the sole ecological process.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Provides a source–sink framework and warns against labeling every oral taxon as contamination; use source–sink/neutral logic if paired reference data become available.
must_not_claim: All BAL taxa derive passively from the mouth, or smoking effects explain this cohort.

citation: Segal LN et al. Enrichment of lung microbiome with supraglottic taxa is associated with increased pulmonary inflammation.
clinical_population: Asymptomatic never-, former-, and current smokers
central_scientific_question: Is supraglottic-taxa enrichment in BAL associated with inflammation?
main_finding: Prevotella/Veillonella-enriched BAL was associated with higher BAL inflammatory cells and exhaled nitric oxide.
conceptual_contribution: Introduced SPT versus background-predominant ecological states with explicit controls.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: A valid oral signal must be externally defined from upper-airway taxa and separated from background signal.
must_not_claim: Our five significant taxa constitute an SPT score, or taxonomic association establishes inflammation.

citation: Bassis CM et al. Analysis of the upper respiratory tract microbiotas as the source of the lung and gastric microbiotas in healthy individuals.
specimen: Oral wash, nasal swab, BAL, gastric aspirate
central_scientific_question: Which upper-airway sites seed the lung and stomach?
main_finding: The mouth was a major source for lung communities, with evidence of selective elimination.
conceptual_contribution: Refined the lung as a dynamic source–sink ecosystem rather than a closed community.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Motivates prospective oral reference sets and within-person similarity measures.
must_not_claim: Oral detection in unpaired BAL identifies microaspiration frequency.

citation: Segal LN et al. Enrichment of the lung microbiome with oral taxa is associated with lung inflammation of a Th17 phenotype.
specimen: Upper airway and acellular BAL; immune and metabolite measurements
clinical_population: Three cohorts without known pulmonary disease
central_scientific_question: Does oral-taxa enrichment correspond to a functional host phenotype?
main_analysis: SPT/BPT classification, cytokines, immune cells, metabolites
main_finding: SPT enrichment tracked Th17/neutrophilic inflammation and a distinct metabolic profile.
conceptual_contribution: Linked an independently motivated oral immigration state to host biology.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Use as biological precedent only if an external oral definition and independent host/functional evidence are used.
must_not_claim: Our taxonomy alone demonstrates Th17 inflammation, metabolic activity, or causal microaspiration.

citation: Dickson RP et al. Bacterial topography of the healthy human lower respiratory tract.
specimen: Seven protected brushes and bilateral BAL per person plus exhaustive controls
central_scientific_question: Does bronchoscopy reflect authentic lower-airway ecology and what is the immigration route?
main_analysis: Topographic biomass, richness, and mouth–lung similarity analyses
main_finding: Mouth–lung immigration indices exceeded control signal and peaked near the carina, consistent with microaspiration.
conceptual_contribution: Provided protected-sampling evidence that mouth–lung resemblance is not simply scope contamination.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Frames aspiration as an ecological inference requiring topography, biomass, and controls.
must_not_claim: Our single BAL per person can distinguish aspiration from procedural carryover.

citation: Drengenes C et al. Laboratory contamination in airway microbiome studies.
specimen: Oral wash, two protected BAL fractions, protected brush, negative controls
central_scientific_question: How much laboratory contamination affects protected lower-airway samples?
main_analysis: Biomass gradients, dilution standards, negative controls, decontam
main_finding: An estimated 10–50% of low-airway profiles could be laboratory-derived; extraction kits were a major source.
conceptual_contribution: Quantified the scale of contamination and favored model-based contaminant handling.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Justifies explicit classified-fraction/QC sensitivity and limits biological claims without matched negatives.
must_not_claim: Low classified fraction is harmless, or computational filtering proves all retained taxa are authentic.

citation: Einarsson GG et al. Microbiomic analysis on low abundant respiratory biomass samples; improved recovery of microbial DNA from BALF.
cohort_size: Analytic sample count varies by extraction experiment
clinical_population: Pediatric chronic lung disease samples and technical tests
central_scientific_question: How do extraction choices affect low-biomass BAL recovery?
main_finding: Laboratory workflow materially changed recovery and inferred community composition.
conceptual_contribution: Shows that processing is part of the biological measurement in BAL.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Use to justify technical sensitivity and cautious between-study comparison.
must_not_claim: Our Kraken/Bracken matrix is directly comparable to 16S BAL studies without workflow harmonization.

citation: Zhong J et al. Benefits and challenges of host depletion methods in profiling the upper and lower respiratory microbiome.
cohort_size: Benchmark study; sample-level n reported in article
central_scientific_question: How do host-depletion methods alter respiratory metagenomes?
main_finding: Depletion increased microbial yield but reduced biomass, introduced contaminants, and altered relative abundance.
conceptual_contribution: Demonstrates method-induced abundance distortion in respiratory shotgun data.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Supports restraint when interpreting relative-abundance differences in highly host-dominated material.
must_not_claim: Published clean-read depth guarantees unbiased microbial composition.

citation: Han D et al. Metagenomic fingerprints in bronchoalveolar lavage differentiate pulmonary diseases.
cohort_size: 402 total; discovery analyses reported for 284 training patients
clinical_population: 123 lung cancer, 114 bacterial infection, 79 fungal infection, 86 TB
central_scientific_question: Can microbial and host mNGS features distinguish cancer from infections?
main_analysis: Alpha/beta diversity, LEfSe, host features, 58/ensemble ML models
main_finding: Reported disease compositional differences; P. micra and P. gingivalis enriched in cancer, F. nucleatum in bacterial infection; integrated test AUC 0.847.
conceptual_contribution: Defines the prior biological and diagnostic claims for PRJNA1056765.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Our work may critique robustness, dispersion, compositionality, QC, and generalizability.
must_not_claim: Disease fingerprints, listed oral taxa, or diagnostic modeling are new discoveries in this dataset.

citation: Tang H et al. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid metagenomic datasets: a multidimensional clinical biomolecular resource.
cohort_size: 402 cases plus 32 DNA and 32 RNA negative controls
sequencing_method: Clinical mNGS with released processed matrices and pipelines
clinical_population: Same cancer/infection cohort as Han et al.
central_scientific_question: Can the cohort and multimodal processing workflows be made reusable?
main_analysis: Technical validation; pipeline and data description
main_finding: Released non-host reads, matrices, negative-control metadata, GSE252118 host expression, Figshare results, and GitHub code.
conceptual_contribution: Establishes data provenance and available independent modalities/controls.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Use its metadata, controls, RNA matrix, and code for reproducibility audits.
must_not_claim: The public 400 DNA runs are an independent cohort or the RNA data are external validation.

citation: Huang YJ et al. The airway microbiome in patients with severe asthma: associations with disease features and severity.
cohort_size: 40 BAL participants in the bronchoscopic arm
central_scientific_question: Do lower-airway communities track asthma severity and inflammatory phenotype?
main_finding: Airway microbial patterns were associated with disease features, with strong dependence on treatment and phenotype context.
conceptual_contribution: Illustrates that diagnosis alone is a coarse explanatory variable.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Frame heterogeneity around measured covariates and phenotype depth.
must_not_claim: A cross-disease BAL association is a disease mechanism without treatment and severity metadata.

citation: Tsay JJ et al. Airway microbiota is associated with upregulation of the PI3K pathway in lung cancer.
journal_year: Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2018
specimen: Lower-airway samples and paired airway/tissue measurements
central_scientific_question: Is lower-airway dysbiosis linked to a host oncogenic pathway?
main_analysis: Microbiome–host pathway association and experimental validation
main_finding: Oral taxa enrichment was associated with airway PI3K signaling; causality required complementary models.
conceptual_contribution: Shows the evidence needed to move from ecology to mechanism.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Borrow the layered taxonomy–host–experiment framework if independent host data are analyzed.
must_not_claim: P. gingivalis or P. micra abundance in our observational data activates PI3K or promotes cancer.

citation: Tsay JJ et al. Lower airway dysbiosis affects lung cancer progression.
sequencing_method: 16S sequencing; host immune profiling; mouse experiments
central_scientific_question: Does oral-taxa-enriched lower-airway dysbiosis associate with prognosis and tumor immunity?
main_finding: SPT enrichment associated with worse outcomes and inflammatory tumor biology.
conceptual_contribution: Strong precedent that oral signals can be clinically relevant, but only with outcome and mechanistic support.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Use as rationale for independently defined SPT-like ecology.
must_not_claim: Our cross-sectional four-diagnosis data support prognosis, tumor progression, or causal oncogenesis.

citation: Dickson RP et al. Lung microbiota predict clinical outcomes in critically ill patients.
journal_year: Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2020
central_scientific_question: Does lower-airway ecology predict outcomes beyond pathogen detection?
main_analysis: Community composition, bacterial burden, clinical-outcome models
main_finding: Enrichment with gut-associated bacteria and higher burden tracked adverse outcomes.
conceptual_contribution: Demonstrates ecological heterogeneity can outperform simple diagnostic categories when outcomes are independent.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Use independent outcomes and burden as validation targets where available.
must_not_claim: Relative taxonomy in our dataset predicts outcome; no outcome data are available.

citation: Fernandes AD et al. Unifying the analysis of high-throughput sequencing datasets: characterizing RNA-seq, 16S rRNA gene sequencing and selective growth experiments by compositional data analysis.
central_scientific_question: How should relative count data be analyzed compositionally?
main_finding: Compositional treatment reduced false interpretation caused by library constraints.
conceptual_contribution: Supports log-ratio sensitivity rather than raw relative-abundance inference alone.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Use CLR/Aitchison and effect-size sensitivity as robustness tools.
must_not_claim: A different method makes a biologically overlapping taxon novel.

citation: Mandal S et al. Analysis of composition of microbiomes: a novel method for studying microbial composition.
journal_year: Microbial Ecology in Health and Disease 2015
central_scientific_question: Can differential taxa be detected while respecting compositional constraints?
main_finding: ANCOM controlled false discoveries under compositional sampling better than naive tests in benchmarks.
conceptual_contribution: Established a differential-abundance approach based on inter-feature log ratios.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Supports prospective compositional differential testing in our cohort.
must_not_claim: ANCOM/CLR significance alone validates biomarkers or mechanisms.

citation: Anderson MJ. Distance-based tests for homogeneity of multivariate dispersions.
central_scientific_question: How can group dispersion be tested separately from centroid/location effects?
main_finding: Provided a permutation test for multivariate dispersion.
conceptual_contribution: Directly explains why our significant Bray PERMANOVA is not an unqualified centroid result.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Pair every PERMANOVA interpretation with dispersion assessment.
must_not_claim: PERMANOVA significance necessarily means disease centroids differ.

citation: Sulaiman I et al. Functional lower airways genomic profiling of the microbiome to capture active microbial metabolism.
specimen: Upper airway, BAL, background controls, SCFA measurements
central_scientific_question: Which assay best captures active lower-airway microbial metabolism?
main_analysis: Cross-omic pathway comparisons and correlation with measured SCFAs; mouse aspiration model
main_finding: Inferred, DNA, and RNA functions differed; WGS/RNA correlated better with SCFAs; RNA best captured transient activity.
conceptual_contribution: Sets a high bar for calling an active microbiome: RNA plus an independent product/host readout.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Use paired DNA–RNA concordance and external functional endpoints as the framework.
must_not_claim: HUMAnN DNA pathways or RNA taxonomic detection alone prove activity or mechanism.

citation: Langelier C et al. Integrating host response and unbiased microbe detection for lower respiratory tract infection diagnosis in critically ill adults.
clinical_population: Critically ill adults with suspected lower respiratory infection
central_scientific_question: Can a single BAL metatranscriptome combine pathogen and host-response evidence?
main_finding: Joint host–microbe information improved discrimination of infection from noninfectious illness.
conceptual_contribution: Shows a genuinely distinct functional direction needs an independent RNA/host question and clinical target.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Use deposited RNA/GSE data only for a prespecified, non-duplicative validation question.
must_not_claim: Rebuilding a classifier in PRJNA1056765 is novel or externally validated.

citation: Sulaiman I et al. Microbial signatures in the lower airways of mechanically ventilated COVID-19 patients associated with poor clinical outcome.
specimen: Lower-airway samples from mechanically ventilated patients
central_scientific_question: Do lower-airway microbial signals associate with outcome and host response?
main_analysis: Microbial burden/composition, host transcriptome, longitudinal outcome associations
main_finding: Poor outcome was associated with altered lower-airway ecology and host–microbe features.
conceptual_contribution: Demonstrates the value of independent outcomes and host response in functional interpretation.
relationship_and_legitimate_framework: Use as a multi-omic design precedent, not as evidence for these four diagnoses.
must_not_claim: Our taxa predict COVID-like outcomes or carry the same mechanism.
